title: 示例教材 · 人教版四年级上册

units.title: Unit 1 Helping at home
patterns: Can you help? - Yes, I can. I can clean my room.
Can she help? - Yes, she can. She can do some chores.
Can he help? - Yes, he can. He can sweep the floor.
Can we help? - Yes, we can. That's for sure!
Is this your father? - Yes, it is. He's a PE teacher.
What's your mother's job? - She's a doctor.
What's your father's job? - He's a factory worker.
What can we do for them? - We can do some chores.
What can you do? - I can sweep the floor. I can cook.
I look after my sister. We sweep the floor. We cook together. We are happy together.
grammar: Modal verb 'can' expressing ability (Subject + can / cannot + base verb; e.g., 'I can clean my room.', 'Can she help? - Yes, she can.')
Asking about occupations using 'What's ... job?' (What's + possessive noun/pronoun + job? - He's/She's a/an + occupation; e.g., 'What's your mother's job? - She's a doctor.')
Simple present tense for habitual actions with 'often' (Subject + often + base verb / verb-s; e.g., 'We often cook together.')
Phonics: 'ch' digraph sounds like /tʃ/ (Rule: the letters 'ch' represent the voiceless affricate /tʃ/; Examples: 'chair', 'China', 'much', 'teacher', 'lunch')
